correctness.rationale: For G_n=K_{n,n} minus the diagonal perfect matching, an undominated edge exists exactly when some unoccupied a_i,b_j have i≠j. Hence domination demands one fully occupied bipartition side or U=V={k}. In the latter case deletion-minimality is equivalent to every selected edge incident to a degree-one endpoint, so the selected graph on 2(n−1) vertices is a star forest. A forest with c components has 2(n−1)−c edges; c≥2, so Γ’≤2n−4; equality forces two opposite-side stars with matching center index ℓ≠k and exactly n(n−1) choices. Minimum size n−1 forces an active deranged perfect matching, exactly nD_{n−1} sets. Other support cases need at least n edges and minimal ones have at most n edges, so n≥5 implies Γ’=2n−4 and γ’=n−1. Independently exhaustively checked all 2^20 edge subsets for n=5, recovering 45 minimizers and 20 maximizers.
